The Exchange Column

Crypto is in a confirmed capitulation phase, and the desk is defensive. Total market capitalization is down 6.34%, and liquidations are lopsided: $166.8M in longs against $16.2M in shorts. Bitcoin has dropped $4,000 in consecutive sessions to break below $76,000, a 5.6% fall over 24 hours. SOL slipped below $90, down 6.7%. Equities offer no shelter, with the S&P 500 down 3% and NVIDIA off over 8%. ETF flows confirm the selling. BTC took in +$74.6M on Wednesday 4 Nov, but its 7-day net is −$752.5M. ETH added +$53.0M that day against a 7-day net of −$515.1M, while SOL logged +$0.0M against −$63.2M over the week. One green day does not reverse a week of outflows. BTC's 1h RSI at 19.32 reads oversold, yet buying volume has not shown up, so sellers are not exhausted. Hyperliquid desks are heavily net short across BTC, ETH and SOL. Lighter whale taker flow shows ETH accumulation of +$11.5M over seven days and BTC distribution of -$1.1M, suggesting capital is rotating toward alts or stablecoins rather than bidding the majors. The regime is RISK_OFF. Continuation shorts carry the momentum. Longs need a real mechanism, such as deeply negative funding, a failed breakdown, or a demand catalyst, not a dip-buy because the chart looks oversold. Dollar liquidity is flat, so trade the price structure on its own merits. Fear and Greed sits at 50, neutral, offering no contrarian signal. Do not trust any bounce until BTC's 7-day net outflow turns.
